templates.notes: Four years (6,800 hours) of practical experience. One month of full-time experience counts as 163 hours. Colorado sets no separate classroom-hour minimum; add your program's classroom target if it has one.

checklist.title: Count months of full-time work as 163 hours
checklist.detail: Colorado treats one month of full-time experience as 163 hours when you document your experience.

templates.notes: Two years (3,400 hours) of practical experience for the residential plumber exam. One month of full-time work counts as 163 hours.
Five full-time years (8,500 hours) of practical experience for the master plumber exam. One month of full-time work counts as 163 hours.

8,000 hours of supervised plumbing installation work while holding an active Idaho apprentice registration, plus 576 hours of instruction at a board-approved apprenticeship program. A work-experience-only pathway also exists.

checklist.title: Keep your Idaho apprentice registration active
checklist.detail: Hours earned in Idaho only count while you hold an active Idaho plumbing apprentice registration.

checklist.title: Finish 576 hours at a board-approved apprenticeship program
checklist.detail: Idaho colleges and training centers on the Plumbing Board's list. You can test after the 576 hours, but the license needs the 8,000 verified work hours too.

checklist.title: Get the Work Verification Form for your 8,000 hours
checklist.detail: The application needs verified, supervised plumbing installation work. Hours can be earned in or out of Idaho.

templates.notes: At least 8,000 hours of on-the-job training before the written and manual journeyman exam. Louisiana Workforce Commission-registered apprenticeships can change the hours; confirm with your sponsor and add classroom hours if your program requires them.

checklist.title: Confirm which path you're on
checklist.detail: Louisiana's board licenses journeymen after 8,000 hours of on-the-job training. Programs registered with the Louisiana Workforce Commission can count differently, so ask your sponsor which one you're in.

templates.board: Board of State Examiners of Plumbers and Gas Fitters
templates.notes: 6,800 clock hours of practical work experience as a licensed apprentice and 550 clock hours of plumbing and gasfitting theory over at least four years (no more than 165 education hours credited per calendar year). 248 CMR 11.02.

checklist.title: Hold a Massachusetts apprentice plumber license
checklist.detail: Hours count when worked as a licensed apprentice under a licensed master plumber, or a journeyman employed by a master.

checklist.title: Start your education within nine months
checklist.detail: Apprentices begin the plumbing education program within nine months of getting their apprentice license (248 CMR 11.02).

checklist.title: Keep education and work in step
checklist.detail: For each year you complete 165 hours of education (1.5 tiers) you need 1,700 hours of qualifying work experience.

checklist.title: Renew your apprentice license every two years
checklist.detail: Apprentice licenses can't be renewed past ten years from the date first granted without Board approval.

checklist.title: Journeyman exam attempts
checklist.detail: You can attempt the journeyman exam up to six times without special Board approval.

templates.board: Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry
templates.notes: Four years of practical plumbing experience as a registered apprentice; one year counts as at least 1,750 hours (4 x 1,750 = 7,000). Minn. R. 4716.0020 also sets minimums for water distribution, DWV and fixture work. Registered apprentices must include 2,000 hours of water distribution, 2,000 of drain/waste/vent and 1,000 of fixture installation inside those hours; the rest can be any plumbing work.

checklist.title: Register as a plumbing apprentice in Minnesota
checklist.detail: The four years of experience must be gained as a registered apprentice. One year counts as at least 1,750 hours.

checklist.title: Track hours by type of work
checklist.detail: Minnesota sets minimum hours for water distribution, drain-waste-vent and fixture installation work (Minn. R. 4716.0020, subp. 2). Tag each entry with a matching category and check the rule for your path.

categoryMinimums.note: Drain, waste and vent system installation

templates.notes: 3,850 hours of commercial and 3,850 hours of residential on-the-job experience, plus 576 hours of academic classroom training (OAR 918-695-0030). Hour Vault tracks the commercial / residential split from your categories.

checklist.title: Finish 576 hours of academic classroom training
checklist.detail: In the subjects listed in OAR 918-695-0030(2)(a). Completing a four-year approved Oregon plumbing apprenticeship also qualifies.

checklist.title: Verify your hours with the Plumbing Experience Verification form
checklist.detail: The division only counts 2,000 hours of work experience per year toward a license (OAR 918-030-0030).

templates.board: Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners (TSBPE)
templates.notes: 8,000 hours under a Responsible Master Plumber while registered as a Plumber's Apprentice (or licensed Tradesman Plumber-Limited), plus the 48-hour TSBPE-approved training or a DOL-approved apprenticeship. A DOL-approved program can credit up to 1,000 OJT hours. Tradesman Plumber-Limited: 4,000 hours + 24-hour training.

checklist.title: Register as a Plumber's Apprentice
checklist.detail: Hours worked before you register don't count. Must be 16 or older, $15 fee, fingerprint background check. A felony conviction needs a Supplemental Criminal History form.

checklist.title: Renew your apprentice registration every year
checklist.detail: The expiration date is printed on your pocket card. TSBPE emails a renewal notice about 65 days before. Only hours worked while your registration is current count.

checklist.title: Get an Employer's Certification Form from every employer
checklist.detail: TSBPE proves your hours with signed Employer's Certification Forms, one per employer. Ask for one each time you leave a job.

checklist.title: Complete the 48-hour TSBPE-approved training
checklist.detail: Or be enrolled in, or finish, a U.S. Department of Labor-approved apprenticeship program. TSBPE lists approved providers on its website.

checklist.title: Apply for the Journeyman Plumber exam
checklist.detail: Send the application, your Employer's Certification Forms and the $40 fee.

templates.notes: Completion of a plumber's apprenticeship education program (576 classroom hours) and 8,000 hours of licensed plumbing experience under a licensed journeyman or master plumber. A 16,000-hour experience-only path also exists.

checklist.title: Work under an apprentice plumber license
checklist.detail: Utah counts licensed plumbing experience under a licensed journeyman or master, plus the 576-hour apprenticeship education program.

checklist.title: Spread hours across the required work areas
checklist.detail: Utah's apprenticeship rule (R156-55c-302b) sets minimum hours for each area of plumbing work. Use categories to track them and confirm the table with your program.

templates.notes: Four years or more (at least 8,000 hours) as a certified plumber trainee under a journey level plumber; at least 4,000 hours must be commercial or industrial. Hours only count while your trainee certificate is current.

checklist.title: Keep your plumber trainee certificate current
checklist.detail: Washington hours aren't credited unless you held a current plumber trainee certificate when you worked them.

checklist.title: Keep your hours documented and signed
checklist.detail: The 8,000 hours must be documented training under a certified journey level plumber.

categoryMinimums.note: At least 4,000 of the 8,000 hours in commercial or industrial installations

templates.notes: Two years or more (at least 4,000 hours) as a plumber trainee under a journey level, residential specialty or residential service plumber. The first 2,000 hours must be under the direct supervision of a journey level or residential specialty plumber.

Three years or more (at least 6,000 hours) working in the specialty as a trainee under a certified residential or journey level plumber. Limited to single-family dwellings, duplexes and apartment buildings of three stories or less.

templates.board: Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development, Mechanical Inspection
templates.notes: 8,000 hours of legally obtained commercial or residential plumbing installation work while holding a Plumber Trainee Certificate of Fitness. Up to 1,000 hours of trade-related classroom training can count toward the 8,000. Maintenance hours do not count. Work in Alaska without a valid trainee certificate is not counted.

templates.board: Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners (TSBPE)
templates.notes: 4,000 hours of plumbing experience while registered as a Plumber's Apprentice, plus a 24-hour TSBPE-approved training course (not needed with an out-of-state journeyman or master license). Limited to one- and two-family dwellings.

At least 2 years and 4,000 hours of plumbing installation work as a licensed trainee plumber under a master plumber. A journeyman-in-training license after a board-approved plumbing course needs 2,000 hours instead; set your own hours if that is your route.

commonChecklist.title: Register or get licensed as an apprentice
commonChecklist.detail: Most boards only count hours worked while you hold a current apprentice registration or license. Register before you start counting hours.

commonChecklist.title: Keep your registration current
commonChecklist.detail: Apprentice registrations expire and have to be renewed. Add your due date and Hour Vault will remind you 30 and 7 days before.

commonChecklist.title: Finish the background check, if your board requires one
commonChecklist.detail: Many boards require fingerprints for a registration or license. A felony conviction can mean extra forms.

commonChecklist.title: Get signed hour verification from every employer
commonChecklist.detail: Boards want proof of your hours signed by the employer or supervisor. Ask for it each time you change jobs and keep a copy.

commonChecklist.title: Keep a certificate or transcript for every class
commonChecklist.detail: Related training hours are usually proven with a certificate or transcript from an approved provider.

commonChecklist.title: Apply for the journeyman exam
commonChecklist.detail: Submit the application, fee and hour documentation once your hours and classes are complete.
